source.rights: John Ryan Foundry, Baltimore, United States, Latest and standard faces in type, printers tools and machinery, published 1894; historical publication in the public domain by age.
source.role: Clearer whole g and independent eight-point optical/scale comparisons.

accepted_physical_scale.method: One isotropic least-squares scale from independently selected common capitals; no target g/dollar, R alternatives or M variants in fit.

accepted_row.method: Whole flat-footed r/b/m/l/n/h shapes anchor Theil-Sen baseline; targets and rounded forms excluded.

selected.decision: The Ryan g in Tumbling, at threshold 175, retains both native counters and a clearer loop junction than the census impression. The g in Vaulting remains comparison evidence because its upper bowl is broken at 175. The independent uniform scale, measured text baseline and italic slant are preserved. The existing 733-unit advance and 35-unit left bearing are retained. No strokes are drawn or assembled from other impressions.

recipe.notes: The Ryan g in Tumbling, at threshold 175, retains both native counters and a clearer loop junction than the census impression. The g in Vaulting remains comparison evidence because its upper bowl is broken at 175. The independent uniform scale, measured text baseline and italic slant are preserved. The existing 733-unit advance and 35-unit left bearing are retained. No strokes are drawn or assembled from other impressions. Four-times Lanczos sampling preserves the native evidence; no hole filling or independent stretching is applied.

comparisons.exclusion_reason: Native A diagonal/I serifs weak; N hairline detached under working threshold. Exclude from scale fit rather than let lost strokes shrink width measurement.
